pattern_name: Modals of deduction (must / might / could / can't)
formula: must + verb (sure it's true) · might / may / could + verb (possible) · can't + verb (sure it's false)
formula_visual: [He must be tired] // [She might be at work] // [That can't be right]
when_to_use: To say how CERTAIN you are about a present situation, based on evidence. must = I'm sure it's true. might/may/could = it's possible. can't = I'm sure it's not true. All are followed by the bare infinitive (no 'to').
when_to_use_ar: للتعبير عن درجة اليقين في موقف حاضر بناءً على دليل. must = متأكد أنه صحيح. might/may/could = ممكن. can't = متأكد أنه غير صحيح. كلها + الفعل المجرد بدون to.
why_arabic_speakers_struggle: Arabic expresses certainty with separate words (لا بد أن، ربما، مستحيل), so learners add 'to' after the modal ('must to be') or use 'mustn't' for impossibility instead of 'can't'.

examples.en: He's been working all day — he must be tired.
examples.ar: يعمل طوال اليوم — لا بد أنه متعب

examples.en: She might be at work now.
That can't be right — check it again.
The keys could be in the car.
They must know each other well.
examples.ar: لا بد أنهما يعرفان بعضهما جيدًا

common_errors.explanation: Modals take the bare infinitive — no 'to'.
For 'I'm sure it's NOT true' we use can't, not mustn't.
'maybe' is an adverb; the modal pattern is might + verb.

practice_fill_blank.sentence: The lights are off. They ___ (be) asleep. (I'm sure)
I'm not certain, but she ___ (be) in the library. (possible)
practice_fill_blank.answer: might be / may be / could be

practice_fill_blank.sentence: That ___ (be) his brother — he's an only child.
He speaks perfect French. He ___ (have) lived in Paris.
It ___ (rain) later, so take an umbrella. (possible)

quick_rule: Sure yes → must. Maybe → might/may/could. Sure no → can't. Always + bare verb (no 'to').
quick_rule_ar: متأكد نعم → must. ربما → might/may/could. متأكد لا → can't. دائمًا + فعل مجرد بدون to.
connect_to_speaking: In accent week 6 you practised must/might/can't in deduction. Say: 'He must be tired' with a falling, confident tone, then 'She might be at work' with a lighter, uncertain tone.
